title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: Which statement correctly separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: A workflow never calls a model, but an agent always does
A workflow uses fewer tools than an agent ever needs to
In a workflow, code sets the steps; in an agent, the model does
In a workflow, the model sets the steps; in an agent, code does

items.stem: Every booking request in the makerspace assistant must (1) check the student's training status, (2) check the calendar for the slot, (3) create the booking, (4) send a confirmation. The steps and their order never change. Who should own the control flow for this part?

options.text: The program, as a fixed workflow, with the model only filling in fields
The model, so that it can reorder the four steps whenever it wants
The model, because every one of the four steps involves calling a tool
A second model that reviews each step the first model decides to take

items.stem: A teammate says: "It uses a language model and several tools, so it is an agent." In one sentence, explain why that alone does not make it an agent.
At the design review, someone asks when a fixed workflow is a better choice than an agent for part of the assistant. Which reason is the strongest?

options.text: Students will find the assistant more flexible and more natural
The team wants the model to handle every kind of request
The sponsor's budget is large, so the cost per request is not an issue
The steps are known in advance and the cost per request must be predictable

items.stem: Suppose each model call costs the same. A fixed workflow for answering a manual question makes exactly 2 model calls per request. An agent doing the same job averages 5 model calls per request, because it loops. Over 300 requests, how many more model calls does the agent make than the workflow?
Which part of the makerspace assistant is the best candidate to be an agent, rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Sending the booking confirmation after a slot is reserved
Answering open troubleshooting questions that may need several manual lookups
Checking the training status before any booking is created
Writing each completed booking to the log in a set format
